<reason>B wins by separating benefits of rooftop solar from benefits attributable to peer trading. B directly challenged what funds simultaneous buyer discounts and higher seller returns, explained how time-varying tariffs also benefit renters, and answered the regulatory-capacity challenge without demanding perfect regulation. A offered plausible investment and bargaining incentives, but repeatedly returned to disputed physical savings and did not establish why its additional benefits outweigh settlement costs and cost-shifting risks.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's strongest response caught A reintroducing avoided distant generation and recovered curtailment after conceding that billing arrangements do not change electricity flows. Existing local consumption already captures the former; contracts alone do not resolve the latter. This directly undermined A's answer about what funds the promised bargain.</best_rebuttal>
